- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true prices often show sharper, more volatile corrections or mean reversion after spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overcorrect or underestimate the subsequent drop, failing to capture the full magnitude of the correction.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 10–15 days of the forecast, then gradually flattens — true prices often show a more pronounced downward trend or mean-reversion pattern after the peak.
- Model fails to account for short-term volatility and sharp corrections, especially after high peaks — true prices often drop more aggressively than forecasted.
- Model underestimates the true price range in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when prices are trending downward or consolidating.
- Model tends to ignore the influence of recent low prices (last 5–7 days) in the forecast, leading to overestimation when the market is recovering from a dip.
- Model shows a lag in adjusting to recent price drops — it often takes 2–3 days to reflect the true downward trend, while true prices adjust faster.
- Model overestimates the mean price in the forecast horizon, especially when the true price is trending downward — it fails to recognize the downward bias in the latter half of the forecast.
